correctness.rationale: The board-to-path bijection is explicit and encoded by a deterministic 18-state three-mask transfer; exact symbolic matrix inversion verifies the bivariate numerator and denominator. An independent cell-covering enumeration checks every histogram through 4-by-9, including the six-column two-square cycle. Strong connectivity and a zero-square length-one loop ensure primitive Perron theory. Two cycles with different squares per step prove positive asymptotic variance via the finite-state coboundary criterion. Analytic perturbation/quasi-powers gives CLT with the stated normalizations; finite tests do not purport to prove asymptotic claims.

originality.rationale: The full primary text of Thorat arXiv:2610.39907v1 (background, §2.10, §3) proves a criterion for cocycle triviality and topological mixing, not an exact square-marked 4-row transfer enumerator. Propp 2001 and Cohn–Kenyon–Propp 2001 treat pure dominoes, so their recurrences and variational principles do not imply the mixed 3-by-3-square square-frequency pressure. Published nearby finite-strip matching records also have different tile sets or homological observables. Precise sequence and alias searches located no covering theorem or table. Priority is provisional; the scientific inference is non-implication by different premises, not novelty from lack of search matches.
residual_risks: Historical priority is provisional; a matching unpublished manuscript or an unindexed integer-sequence table may exist.

Finite-state rational-function and central-limit machinery are classical; originality is limited to the particular marked mixed-strip computation and resulting explicit asymptotic invariants.

value.rationale: The first interacting four-row strip of the natural primitive {horizontal domino, vertical domino, 3-by-3 square} tile family is qualitatively outside the height-three renewal regime: the large tile leaves a lane allowing crossing dominoes. Its exact pressure, asymptotic 3-by-3-square frequency and strictly positive Gaussian variance answer natural quantitative questions of the strip dynamical system not implied by the full-plane cohomological criterion or pure-dimer formulas. It supplies a reproducible finite-width benchmark but makes no unproved full-plane claims.
